answer: An agent marketplace grants one request per hour for each token locked in escrow for 30 days. Agents selling lantern designs, opal appraisals, or nectar delivery all face the same rule. Splitting a deposit among a thousand identities yields no more total requests than keeping it under one name. To flood the market, an attacker must acquire and lock proportionally more tokens, tying up capital for a month instead of gaining capacity by inventing names.
